notes: Accessed hvlgroup.com directly via Chrome (HTTP 200 on every route); robots.txt is a 404 (no Claude-specific disallow), consistent with the prior Home-Decor pass's finding (archive c258/notes/216.md). hvlgroup.com is Hudson Valley Lighting Group's shared multi-brand storefront (Hudson Valley Lighting, Troy, Corbett, Mitzi, Schoolhouse, Sonneman, CSL) -- it is primarily a lighting manufacturer, but the prior pass explicitly flagged that it excluded 'Tables/Chairs-Stools/Storage-Furniture/Beds (furniture)' from its decor extraction per standing Home-Decor scope rules; this pass recovers exactly that excluded set. Tree source: the site's own nav ('New Furnishings' -> /Products/SuperCategory/Furniture, an 'All Furniture' catch-all listing 81 products, all branded SCHOOLHOUSE -- confirmed a genuine furniture sub-brand making tables, chairs, stools, cabinets, bookshelves, storage carts and beds) plus the site's own Category checkbox facet on that page, which enumerates exactly 6 category values for the Furniture supercategory: Beds, Cabinet, Seating, Storage Carts, Storage Furniture, Tables. All 6 map to their own clean /Products/Category/<slug> listing URLs (same in-house ASP.NET MVC catalog pattern verified for lighting in the prior pass) and were fetched directly. Excluded per SS3: /Products/SuperCategory/Furniture and /Products/Feature/Furniture, both literally labelled 'All Furniture' on-page -- catch-all pages, never extracted as rows, used only as tree/count source. Also excluded: /Products/Room/Bedroom and the other 7 Room-tree nodes -- the prior pass proved empirically (shared SKU C2140-VGL appearing as both the first Chandelier-category item and the first Bedroom-room item, plus Bedroom containing 60% of the whole 8080-item catalog) that Room pages are a pure facet re-cut of the entire catalog, not a genuine separate branch; that finding is architecture-level (same ASP.NET MVC catalog engine, same Room-tag mechanism) and applies identically here, so Room nodes were not walked again. Qty method: for every one of the 6 category pages, the rendered 'N Products' header text and the page's own hidden TotalObjectCount form field agreed exactly (28/28, 8/8, 13/13, 31/31, 14/14, 4/4) -- same first-party DB-count corroboration method the prior pass established as exact for this site (not a Shopify/Algolia estimate). Cross-listing / overlap, documented not flagged: Cabinet's 4 itemcodes (all 'Forma Cabinet' colorways, SH146309-*) are an exact subset of Storage Furniture's 31 itemcodes; Storage Carts' 13 itemcodes (all 'Miller Storage Cart'/'Lolly Bar Cart', SH146354/SH146359/SH142632/SH146223) are also an exact subset of Storage Furniture's 31. This is the identical cross-listing behavior the prior pass documented for the Lighting side of this same site ('a lantern-style chandelier appears under both Chandelier and Lantern') -- Storage Furniture, Storage Carts and Cabinet are presented as three flat, independently-browsable sibling nodes in the site's own Category facet (not a nested tree), each with its own distinct URL and headline count, so per the established site-taxonomy precedent all 6 are emitted as flat leaf rows with no artificial grouping row, exactly as the prior pass did for the flat Pendant/Chandelier/Lantern siblings. No furniture leaf reads 0 or absurdly low so no stock-gating concern was flagged. Sanity checks: h1 element was empty/absent on every category page (site quirk, not a wrong-category signal) so identity was confirmed instead via URL slug + on-page product titles matching the expected type (e.g. Beds page shows 'Hamilton Bed' SKUs, Tables page shows Andy/Ann/Owen/Darrow side/coffee/dining tables) -- no bad-slug/parent-fallback pattern observed. Excluded per standing furniture/decor scope: Bedding (textile), Wall-Hardware/Mirrors/Decorative-Accessories (decor, not furniture -- these belong to the Home-Decor project, already captured there), Pulls/Knobs (hardware), Bulbs, and all lighting fixture types.
